small_guidance:
- The post kernel is already cheap (~0.5ms class); the ConvTranspose3d dominates the 11.1ms runtime. Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps on the post kernel will not move fast_p meaningfully — focus must shift to the conv.
- If keeping the current structure, try BLOCK_S=2048 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3 to coalesce more work per program, and ensure the bias scalar is passed as a constexpr-baked value (load once outside the kernel into a register-resident scalar).
- Make sure x is in channels_last_3d so the C-axis loads in the LSE are contiguous — currently strided by SPATIAL which hurts memory throughput.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and `atomic_add`ing into the output grid at `(d*stride - pad + kd, h*stride - pad + kh, w*stride - pad + kw)`. Output shape is [128,16,31,63,63].
- Alternatively, since stride=2/padding=1/kernel=3 produces a regular pattern, implement as a gather-style direct kernel: one program per output tile, iterating only over the (kd,kh,kw) positions whose input index `(o + pad - k)/stride` is integral — avoids atomics entirely and is the preferred design on a 4090.
- Fuse the LSE-over-channels + HardSwish + bias-sub + clamp epilogue directly into the conv-transpose kernel by accumulating all OC outputs in registers per output spatial point, then reducing across OC immediately before storing the single-channel result — this eliminates writing/reading the 16-channel intermediate (~64MB) entirely.
